sentences.text: The controlled slot swap process begins when an Aircraft Operator Representative identifies a flight that can exchange its assigned demand position without reducing declared capacity or creating an unfair priority change.
The Airline Operations Coordinator enters the proposed substitution in the Airport CDM Portal with the flight identifiers, operational reason, readiness basis, and requested effective time.
The Airport CDM Portal validates the submitting user through the Identity Access Service and blocks any proposal from a party without delegated operator authority.

The Slot Allocation Engine evaluates the candidate swap against active Ground Delay Program constraints, Calculated Takeoff Time integrity, Target Off Block Time dependencies, and Airport Acceptance Rate commitments.
The Business Rules Registry provides the governing parameters for precedence, equity, customs eligibility, minimum notification time, and prohibited trades.
The Slot Coordinator reviews any exception raised by the Slot Allocation Engine and confirms whether the swap remains consistent with regional flow objectives.
Slot Coordinator sends the Slot Swap Permission Email only after the governance checks have been completed and recorded.
For airline-to-airline coordination, each Aircraft Operator Representative records concurrence in the Airport CDM Portal rather than relying on a verbal agreement.
The Network Operations Liaison monitors aggregate displacement from approved substitutions to ensure that one carrier's recovery action does not destabilize the wider network plan.
The Regional Flow Manager may suspend collaborative substitution during a Capacity Reduction State when scarce capacity must be protected for the published tactical plan.
The Tower Supervisor retains authority to reject a swap if the resulting sequence would conflict with safe runway sequencing or local control workload.
The Ramp Control Lead confirms that the revised sequence remains compatible with stand occupancy, pushback spacing, and tug availability shown on the Ramp Movement Board.
Airport Duty Manager uses the Apron Sweep Completion Note to confirm that apron availability constraints do not invalidate an approved substitution.
Airline Operations Coordinator uses the release note to confirm that a candidate substitution is eligible for customs release before requesting a slot swap.
Customs release status is treated as a prerequisite condition for any substitution that would move an international departure into an earlier operating position.
If customs status is incomplete, the Airport CDM Portal keeps the proposal pending and prevents the Slot Allocation Engine from publishing the revised slot assignment.
The Collaborative Decision Log captures the proposed flights, the reason code, the user confirmations, the governance outcome, and the final decision time.
The Audit Event Ledger records each approval, rejection, cancellation, and override so that later review can distinguish operational judgment from system enforcement.
The Flight Data Exchange publishes revised Flight Intent Message content only after the approved substitution is final and time synchronized.
The Common Situation Display presents the updated Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time so that operational users share the same view of the accepted change.
The Departure Metering Service recalculates metering advisories after approval and prevents the swap from creating a new demand peak at a departure fix.
Disputes between operators are escalated to the Regional Flow Manager when the recorded concurrences conflict or when a party alleges that governance rules were bypassed.
The System Support Engineer investigates technical failures in submission, validation, or publication without altering the operational decision unless authorized through the defined control process.
The Post Operations Report includes swap volume, rejection reasons, approval latency, compliance with revised times, and any equity concerns identified during the operating period.
